The core data structure is a 3D texture array or a 4D texture representation where the fourth dimension represents the mipmap level.
**Voxelization:** Rasterize scene geometry into a 3D texture.
This process averages the values in adjacent voxels to create lower-resolution levels.
*   **Opacity and Shadowing Loss:** Linear pre-filtering does not preserve accurate transparency.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** The position calculation assumes the scene fits within `scene_size`.
*   **Time Complexity:** Mipmap generation is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels in the base level, assuming a fixed number of mipmap levels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the full mipmap chain, increasing memory usage by approximately 33% over the base texture (sum of geometric series $1 + 1/4 + 1/16 + \dots$).
Compute Shaders may offer more control but require additional implementation overhead.
Voxel Pre-integration was introduced as part of the Voxel Cone Tracing technique for real-time global illumination.
It builds upon the concept of using voxelized lighting data to approximate indirect illumination.
